relations.subject: Graves Chamney Haughton
relations.evidence: entered Fort William College in Calcutta to further his knowledge of oriental languages, winning several prizes. Ill-health caused by over-exerting himself in study caused him to return home in 1815.

relations.subject: Graves Chamney Haughton
relations.evidence: Two years later, he was appointed as an assistant professor at the East India College, Haileybury;

relations.subject: Graves Chamney Haughton
relations.evidence: he held the post of professor of Sanskrit and Bengali from 1819 to 1827

relations.subject: Graves Chamney Haughton
relations.evidence: including the Royal Asiatic Society which he helped to found.

relations.subject: Graves Chamney Haughton
relations.evidence: when he attempted in 1832 to be elected as the first Boden Professor of Sanskrit, but he stood down from the contest in favour of Horace Hayman Wilson
